subject: Request: 90d targeted retention for debug traces - LynxCloud SOC 2 / SIG ask
messages:
From: Danielle Park <dani@lynxcloud.io>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: LynxCloud Security <security@lynxcloud.io>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: 90d targeted retention for debug traces

Hi Sergio / Marissa,

Following up from our compliance review: LynxCloud is requesting a customer-specific retention exception for debug traces tied to our tenant for a period of 90 days (vs the default 30d ephemeral window). The ask is driven by a regulatory requirement in one of our verticals — we need the ability to pull full debug traces for incident forensics up to 90 days after an event.

Can Redwood support a targeted retention carveout for the following tenant(s)? I attached our standard retention request form (lynx-retention-request-form.pdf). We also need evidence for the SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ mapping showing:
- where the retained traces will reside (encrypted storage)
- access controls and audit logs for retrieval
- deletion workflow after the 90d window

Desired tenants: lynx-prod-1, lynx-analytics-01
Desired start: as soon as contract amendment executed; target implementation within two weeks if possible.

Appreciate a short reply with whether this is feasible, a proposed implementation plan, and any additional artifacts you need.

Thanks,
Danielle Park
Senior Security Operations
LynxCloud

Attachment: lynx-retention-request-form.pdf (application/pdf, 210 KB)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Danielle Park <dani@lynxcloud.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: 90d targeted retention for debug traces

Hi Danielle — thanks for the clear ask and the form. Looping in Ben from Security/Infra to scope the implementation and Marissa for contract/ops coordination.

High-level thoughts:
- We can do tenant-scoped targeted retention (90d) for debug traces, but we need to pick an implementation mode (tenant-scoped encrypted bucket vs. extended retention on the serving runtime). Each has tradeoffs on cost and access control.
- We will provide SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ artifacts showing the control points (storage, KMS, audit logs).
- We'll need a signed amendment (DocuSign) to include the retention exception and any billing uplift.

Ben — can you confirm the recommended approach and an ETA? Marissa — can you prepare a redlined amendment template and ballpark uplift so Danielle can review with procurement? I attached a short plan draft (redwood-targeted-retain-plan.docx).

Sergio
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-targeted-retain-plan.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 46 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Danielle Park <dani@lynxcloud.io>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: 90d targeted retention for debug traces

Sergio / Marissa / Danielle —

Thanks for the heads up. Technical summary and proposed approach below.

Proposal (recommended): create a tenant-scoped encrypted object store for the specified tenants (lynx-prod-1, lynx-analytics-01) with a 90-day retention policy. Key details:
- Storage: S3-compatible object store in the same region (us-west-2) with server-side encryption (AES-256) and customer-managed KMS keys.
- Access: Role-based access limited to LynxCloud Security and Redwood Forensics team; retrieval via signed, time-limited presigned URLs logged to our audit pipeline.
- Auditability: All access and admin actions pushed to a dedicated audit log stream; we can provide the audit log slices as SOC 2 artifact.
- Deletion: Automated lifecycle rule to hard-delete after 90 days; we will provide a deletion manifest and a signed proof-of-delete for each retention window.
- Isolation: Data will be tenant-tagged and shredded from caches; no cross-tenant mixing.

Estimated effort / timeline: 6–8 business days to stand up the tenant buckets, configure KMS and audit sinks, and validate retrieval/test playbook.

Compliance artifacts we can provide: configuration screenshots, CAIQ control mapping export, SOC 2 audit artifact template, and a short attestation letter for the specific exception. I attached the CAIQ mapping export (caiq-mapping.zip).

Notes / open items:
1) Contract amendment/DocuSign to authorize the exception and billing uplift (Marissa to draft).
2) Clear list of tenant IDs and confirmation that only those two tenants require the 90d window.
3) If LynxCloud requires additional retention (beyond 90d) or broader scope we should evaluate Dedicated capacity which is more cost-effective for long-tail retention.

Sergio / Ben / Marissa —

Appreciate the quick turn. The proposed approach sounds good and acceptable to our security and legal teams. Confirming:
- Tenants: lynx-prod-1, lynx-analytics-01 (final).
- Implementation ETA: 6–8 business days is fine; target window aligns with our incident readiness schedule.
- We will sign the amendment — procurement has prepared DocuSign and I can route once Marissa sends the redline. Link below for reference: https://docs.docusign.com/s/lynxcloud-amendment-lc4021

Two quick asks:
1) Can Redwood provide a short attestation letter (on company letterhead) mapping the retention exception to the relevant CAIQ controls? We need that for our next auditor check.
2) Please include an estimated monthly uplift for the 90d retention (per-GB) so procurement can approve the DocuSign quickly.

If those two items are deliverable in parallel with implementation we’ll kick off DocuSign today.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the amendment and the uplift number.

Danielle
Senior Security Operations, LynxCloud
